newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: IAEA makes progress on nuclear liability deal.
newsitem.headline: IAEA makes progress on nuclear liability deal.

text.p: The International Atomic Energy Agency said on Friday an international committee of experts had made unexpected progress in drawing up new guidelines on setting liability payments for civil nuclear accidents.
A spokesman for the United Nations nuclear watchdog said the special committee, which has met at intervals for the past four years, had produced a draft document for member governments to consider.
"This is a very promising step, it is a big step," IAEA spokesman Hans Meyer told Reuters. "Now it is up to the governments to decide whether the proposals are acceptable."
Under the draft document, victims of a nuclear accident would receive damages quickly and Western investment in ageing East European nuclear plants would be made easier.
The proposals provide for a maximum liability of around $450 million for each nuclear power plant. An international fund would provide an additional $450 million in the event of a nuclear accident.

Meyer said the standing committee would meet again in February 1997 after governments had studied the proposals. Given a consensus, the Board of Governors would adopt the protocol at a scheduled meeting in March, 1997.
Liability for civil nuclear accidents is now regulated by Vienna and Paris conventions.

But existing arrangements have drawn criticism as being too vague. Some nations fear they may miss out on liability payments altogether, while others worry that they could be hit by an enormous bill if there is a nuclear accident.
